floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 17 is PURE register-rename — build emits all 170 insns in target's exact order; gap is exactly two allocation ties ($t1/$t2 and $v1/$a1); three ordering/spelling levers killed with measur

cc1 -da allocation dump turned this into a solvable simulation: loop1's ENTIRE register seating now equals target, s1's 'v1 must stay shared' constraint is overturned, and the whole residual is confin

Floor 17 -> 5: m2c's goto-shaped loop2 denied its pseudos loop_depth reference weighting; rewriting loop2 as real loops (row pointer compiler-made, row counter shared with loop1's a3) makes loop1+loop

frontier.hypothesis: Tie A closes with a spelling of 'the 0x2C00 store is emitted twice but reads t2's pseudo once' that costs no instruction. This is the ONLY remaining defect: floor 5, and all five diffs are tie A.
frontier.mechanism: priority = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs/live_length. t2 at 5 refs / 150 insns = 0.0667 beats t1val at 3 / 76 = 0.0395 and takes the lower $t1; t2 at 3 / 150 = 0.020 loses to it, and an EXACT tie also wins because allocno numbering favours t1val (76 < 83). t2's length is double t1val's purely because t2 is live on both arm paths while t1val is dead along the a3>=5 path.
frontier.next_probe: Already dead and not to be re-run: two-ifs factoring (171), condition cached in a local (171), literal in both arms (170 but CSE rebuilds one pseudo, seating unchanged), literal in one arm only (171, score 3 -- closest miss), v0 copy (171), 's0[1] = t2;' hoisted with 's0 += 2' (167). Untried: express the two arms so their duplicated stores come from ONE source sequence that cc1 cross-jumps or tail-duplicates; and attack t1val's live_length downward instead -- with 3 refs it needs length <= 45 against its current 76, so anything that confines t1val to fewer basic blocks wins. Beware the alias-rename cheat family: a second C handle for the same value under a different name is NOT an allowed lever. Screen every form on the .lreg/.greg numbers with s3/sweep2.py before scoring.

frontier.hypothesis: F5's original suggestion -- re-express loop1's two arms from the primitive layout rather than as two duplicated literal store runs -- is now the most promising untried direction, and it is a rederive-modality job.
frontier.mechanism: The arms store {s3val, t2, s1val, -0xC1, -0x100, -0x3FC1, -0x4000} and {s2val, t2, t1val, -0x40C1, -0x4100, -0x7FC1, -0x8000}: the SECOND element is t2 in both and the negative constants differ by exactly 0x4000 between arms (which looks like a semi-transparency/tpage bit). A layout-driven expression changes t2's and t1val's reference counts wholesale, which is precisely the quantity tie A turns on -- and unlike the factoring probes it need not add a branch.
frontier.next_probe: In a rederive session, rewrite the arms from the 11-halfword primitive layout (tpage, clut, uv pairs) with the arm difference expressed as data rather than as two store runs, then read the .greg dispositions for t1val/t2 and check build_insns is still 170. Hold fixed everything s3 established: loop2 real loops, row pointer and inner pointer compiler-made, a0 and a3 shared with loop1, loop1's inner loop left goto-shaped, pre-loop order a3/t2/a0.

frontier.hypothesis: The s3 loop-note finding generalises to the rest of the queue and is worth a project-level rule rather than more sessions on this function.
frontier.mechanism: m2c goto-shaped loop bodies get no loop_depth reference weighting, so their register-allocation priorities are systematically wrong; two full sessions were spent on this function searching inside a shape that could not produce target's ordering. Any queue item that is a verbatim m2c transcription with goto-driven loops has the same defect.
frontier.next_probe: Raise with the owner as a candidate .claude/rules entry or memory (alongside register-alloc-pure-c), with this function as the worked example: floor 17 flat across two sessions, then 17 -> 5 in one session once the loops were made real.
